title: bug: providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts fails on HEAD: codexDescriptor.proxyCommand still pins ps1 `command = "node"`, which 0863b6c6 replaced with `command = "$nodeForToml"`
description:
Found by task-97740aed's full daemon snapshot gate. A pure `git archive 17ff3749` (no overlay) fails src/providers/providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts "each side-specific literal is at its own construction site...": `config.proxyCommand: "command = \"node\"" missing from the codex branches + config writer of scripts/moe-agent.ps1`.
Cause: 0863b6c6 (task-64809b19, MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED node pin) changed moe-agent.ps1's codex config writer (:1210, :1503) to `command = "$nodeForToml"`, but codexDescriptor.ts proxyCommand.onlyInPowershell (and its `powershell:` prose, ~:362-366) still names the hardcoded `command = "node"`.
Fix: update the descriptor fact (and the bash/ps1 divergence wording) to match the pinned-interpreter form; daemon-only, no wrapper edit. Every snapshot full-suite gate is red until it lands.
definitionOfDone: codexDescriptor.ts proxyCommand.onlyInPowershell/powershell describe the `command = "$nodeForToml"` form the ps1 codex writer now emits (parity with moe-agent.sh stays explained).
providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts passes on a git-archive snapshot of the landed tree, with the full daemon suite counts in the completion evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
Bring the descriptor fact to the launcher (DoD 1); daemon-only. Edit only packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/codexDescriptor.ts with the Edit tool (customRule). Touch neither wrapper nor providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts: no assertion may be removed or loosened.

First re-anchor on the bytes in your worktree:
- `grep -nF 'command = "$nodeForToml"' scripts/moe-agent.ps1` must show a line inside `function Write-MoeCodexConfig {`. At target 091c7dd0 that is :1228, inside the writer that opens at :1186.
- `grep -cF nodeForToml scripts/moe-agent.sh` must print 0.
- If a later landing changed what Write-MoeCodexConfig emits on its command line, use that literal instead and say so in complete_step.

In the config.proxyCommand fact (~:360-368), change three strings:
1. onlyInPowershell becomes ['command = "$nodeForToml"', 'args = ["$proxyScriptForToml"]']. Only the first literal changes. It replaces 'command = "node"', which 0863b6c6 (task-64809b19) removed from the ps1 writer.
2. powershell becomes: 'command = "$nodeForToml": the node pinned under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED ($script:MoeNode, forward slashes), else bare node; args is always emitted'. Source: ps1 :537-540 sets $script:MoeNode only when $script:MoeRuntimeProtected; the writer builds $nodeForToml from it, else 'node'.
3. divergenceReason becomes: 'The bash writer resolves the proxy command (node plus the script, or a direct proxy binary with no args line); the PowerShell writer always runs node -- the MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED pin, else bare node -- with the proxy script as args. The two wrappers can emit structurally different [mcp_servers.moe] blocks for the same project.' This keeps the parity explanation: bash's TOML_PROXY_CMD is NODE_CMD plus TOML_PROXY_ARGS, or a direct PROXY_CMD with the args line omitted.

The bash prose, onlyInBash, every other fact and every emitterEvidence entry stay byte-identical. The simulated diff is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/8c40a8fe-plan/simulated-fix.diff (a suggestion).

The dated spike record docs/plans/2026-09-11-provider-registry-spike.md:52 still says PowerShell hardcodes node. Leave it: it is a historical plan, and the DoD scopes this row to the descriptor.

Error handling: this is a data-only change with no runtime path. The contract test's problem list is the failure surface. It is red on HEAD with exactly one problem (config.proxyCommand: "command = \"node\"" missing from the codex branches + config writer of scripts/moe-agent.ps1), and that is this task's RED proof; quote it in complete_step from your own snapshot run.
implementationPlan.note: Re-anchored: ps1 :1228 emits command = "$nodeForToml"; moe-agent.sh has 0 nodeForToml. Changed only powershell, onlyInPowershell[0], divergenceReason in config.proxyCommand.

(a) The contract test file and both wrappers are unchanged; `git diff --stat` shows only codexDescriptor.ts.
(b) The new literal is checked in both directions by the existing test: present at the ps1 codex site (codex branches + Write-MoeCodexConfig) and absent from the whole comment-stripped moe-agent.sh.
(c) The powershell prose matches both branches of $nodeForToml (protected pin vs bare node), and the divergenceReason still explains why the two [mcp_servers.moe] blocks can differ.

(e) No other fact's evidence was touched, so emitter pinning and site scoping stay as strong as before.

Rejected: it weakens the contract test, which every earlier descriptor-fix row was told not to do. 3) Also edit the dated spike plan doc. Rejected: it is a historical record outside the DoD.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts checks each onlyInPowershell literal for presence in the comment-stripped codex branches plus `function Write-MoeCodexConfig {` (through the next flush-left `}`), and for absence from the whole comment-stripped moe-agent.sh. The ps1 grok writer emits "command = `\"$nodeForToml`\"" with backticks, so the codex literal stays unique there and is outside the site anyway. A full daemon suite needs a WHOLE-repo archive, because many tests read docs/, scripts/ and .gitignore (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
